name: A new TC with only the guide
summary: I came to the desk the way a new Transition Concierge would, with only The Evening Desk and the playbook's section e, and did the evening's tasks on Ashworth (probate, 9601), Hale (living, 9602) and fresh full houses (9700, and a 9800 estate of 300 lines). Scripts and output are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/NEW. The routine the guide teaches mostly holds. One confirm on Name N shots runs Agent One, the room check and Agent Two with no further presses. Each × Qty does its arithmetic. Record the signed request handles a missing co-representative honestly. The iPad sign-out refuses a tap and files its own PDF. The ratification path does what the guide says. The worst problems are in what a reader receives, not in the presses. A line with no name and no value can be ticked Reviewed, by itself or with Mark reviewed, without any question. The Estate Inventory then prints "REVIEWED — all 9 items" over a blank line and a total that leaves three lines out without saying so. A room-check double that both lines' ticks swept past also prints REVIEWED, so the item is counted twice. The release request the fiduciaries sign carries agent values nobody reviewed, with no IN PROGRESS mark, though the guide says every paper is marked. After a pending-appraisal bequest is signed out to the beneficiary, the desk still offers to hand it to the appraiser. Close job's question names rooms and the ledger. It does not name undecided or unnamed lines, unapproved releases (a living client's shotgun included), the unsigned Contents Record, or an hourly job with no hours logged. I closed Hale with all of those open. Some tasks cannot be found from the guide at all. Sending the inventory package to counsel lives only on the dashboard, and the desk points to it only from inside the folded Job Admin card. Several confirms and playbook passages still describe the agents as they were before 25 October. The living desk tells the TC the appraisal date is "usually the date of death". Accuracy should win here. Ticking reviewed, the REVIEWED stamp and the close question should all be asked against completeness (named, valued, no open duplicate, approvals on record). Each should be a flag naming the lines, never a block.
works_well: Name N shots is one confirm. Agent One, the room check and Agent Two then run by themselves (02_name.js: identify ×2, roomCheck, value ×2, no further presses). The work bar then summarises the run in three lines: '24 named · 2 extra lines from split frames · 2 with nothing in frame', 'Room check: nothing photographed twice', 'Agent Two: 24 valued'.
Each × Qty = Total works as the guide says. Qty 8→12 kept Each at $40 and made Total $480. Typing Each $25 made Total $300 (03_review.js).
A rename by the TC is valued again by itself, researched (the re-value request carried mode 'comps', nameChecked true), and the name the TC typed stays (03_review.js).
+ Another item in this photo adds one blank row and never opens the camera. Name 1 shot then reappears on the work bar for it (04_split_drawer.js).
Remove lines across a selection is one confirm naming each line, with the promise that no photograph is deleted (04_split_drawer.js).

Send request: the Gmail draft names every fiduciary and copies counsel. The card's states (drafted, sent, partly signed, every line approved) read correctly. 'Changed after the draft' and Discard draft work as the guide describes (05_request.js, 11_claims.js).

Record the signed request opens on exactly the request's open lines, pre-ticked. A one-signer save says plainly 'Nora Ashworth has not signed yet: these lines stay on the next request'. The second signature completes the lines and unlocks the sign-outs (05b_record.js, 05c_signout.js).

The iPad sign-out refuses a tap ('Sign the sheet first: a signature, not a tap.'). It prints each line's written approvals with their days, and its acknowledgement says what it does not decide (05c_signout.js, 13_person.js).
The ratification path matches the guide. A line set Distribute with a Date of Disposition before signature is listed apart under 'Already released: for ratification' (14b_ratify.js).
Typing the appraiser's figure in Total makes it the appraisal, at the date of death, with the appraiser as source. File the report clears 'report not filed' (06_appraisal.js).
Close job's refusal opens the Closing bar behind the alert and names every unrated vendor (07_close.js).
A Look at this goes quiet exactly as the guide says: only once every line off its photograph is reviewed (15_look.js).
measurements: Presses per typical agent-named line: 2 (choose Where it goes, tick Reviewed). Add 1 to 2 for a recipient (type, Tab), 1 per wrong name and 1 per wrong count. Counted while driving 03_review.js.
A drawer shot piece by piece, 5 lines made into one: 7 actions (4 row ticks, Remove lines, its confirm, rename the kept line). The kept line keeps only the whisk's photograph (04_split_drawer.js).

Release round trip with one co-representative missing: Send request 1, I've sent it 1, Record the signed request 1, tick signer 1, date 1, Record approval 1, File the signed request 1 (file chooser), Done 1 = 8 presses. The second signer's night is 7 more (05b_record.js, 05c_signout.js).
iPad sign-out for one charity line: 3 presses plus the signature (Sign out 1 to …, overwrite 'Signed by' (it is pre-filled with the firm's name, not the driver's), Sign and file) (05c_signout.js).

Finding what blocks Ashworth's close took 4 places: the alert (vendors only), the confirm after rating (midpoint, ledger, rooms), the Closing bar (receipts, statements) and Job Admin (8 derived lines). None of them names the 3 undecided lines or the 3 unapproved releases (07_close.js, 07b_close.js, 17_jobadmin.js).

Full desk redraw per Reviewed tick on a 300-line estate: 382 ms. Choosing Where it goes 353 ms, a Qty edit 216 ms, renderInventoryTab 339 ms. All at 1440 px in headless Chromium on this machine (19_perf.js). renderInventoryTab alone was 103 ms at 1024 px (23_pickup_reach.js).

Page height with 300 lines: 27,120 px at 1440 (27 screens). The Releases bar starts at 28,090 px at 1024×1366, i.e. 20.6 iPad screens below the top, and the Goodwill Sign out button is at 28,377 px (23_pickup_reach.js).
Naming 24 unnamed shots through the stub took 4.3 s end to end, including the automatic room check and Agent Two (02_name.js).
Controls on the desk that send the inventory package to counsel: 0. The only pointer is a line inside the folded Job Admin card that says to use the dashboard (08_package.js, 17_jobadmin.js).
verifier_note: This report is trustworthy. I wrote six scripts of my own on the frozen copy, all under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/NEW-verify/ (v1_ashworth.js to v6_papers.js, logs in out/v1.log to out/v6.log). They pressed the real controls and reproduced every defect, inconsistency and accuracy claim I could drive: NEW-01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 07, 08, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 19, 23 and 24. I checked the rest against the source and the documents. The fixtures can all be reached in the field: step99's seed, an unnamed shot, agent-named lines, approvals recorded through Record the signed request, iPad sign-outs drawn on the pad. Three things need correcting. My agentValue stub returned a category on an ordinary lot, which the server blanks (main-sync.gs:4746). So NEW-10's category half stands on the code alone. Its condition half I observed. NEW-26 says 'equal weight', but Record the signed request is the filled bronze button and Send request is the outline one. NEW-18's 0.35 s per tick did not reproduce here: renderInventoryTab took 84 ms of script time on 300 lines at 1024 px. That every tick redraws the whole desk is confirmed. Two proposals run into Domain rules: NEW-08 (P28, the iPad donation sheet is the charity receipt) and NEW-24 (P19, a receipt is owed once the approval is complete). Two findings are partly already known: NEW-09's behaviour, and NEW-15's notice landing far from the press. I re-rated several severities down. NEW-01 stays fix-now: the Estate Inventory reports no floor and prints REVIEWED over an unnamed line.

findings.title: A line with no name and no value can be ticked Reviewed, and the inventory then prints REVIEWED over it
findings.where: Row's Reviewed box and the bulk bar's Mark reviewed. invLineReviewed (havellin.html:37222) returns true on r.reviewed alone. _invStampLineReviewed (37229) and _invSetReviewed (37258) accept any line. _invBulkApply 'reviewed' (37355). _invProgressStamp (30613) prints REVIEWED once _invReviewStats.complete holds.
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/24_tick_blank.js: on Ashworth's unnamed photograph #26 the Reviewed box is enabled. One press sets reviewed=true with no question, and the chips read 'Unnamed shots 1 · Not reviewed 3'. audit/NEW/12b_mark.js: Select all on Not yet decided, then Mark reviewed, stamped #26 (no name) and #20/#23 (no value, no disposition). The only notice was '3 items marked reviewed. ⚠ 2 of them were marked unsure'. audit/NEW/12c_allrev.js: after Mark reviewed on every group, the Estate Inventory PDF reads 'REVIEWED — all 9 items' over '26 | — | Dining Room | … | — | not stated', with 3 lines Not yet decided and 'Total estimated fair market value: $8,350'. Nothing says the total leaves out 3 unvalued lines.
findings.tc_impact: On the evening the TC sweeps a room with Select all → Mark reviewed, as the playbook teaches for the repetitive stuff. Blank photographs and undecided lines are swept in silently. The attorney or trust officer then receives a schedule stamped REVIEWED that has an unidentified line on it and a total that is really a floor. That is the opposite of 'nothing claimed'.
findings.proposal: Make Reviewed mean identified. The row's box stays disabled on a line with no name (title 'Name it first'). Mark reviewed skips such lines and names them in its notice ('#26 has no name: left unreviewed'). _invProgressStamp prints REVIEWED only when every line is reviewed and named. Otherwise it prints 'REVIEWED — 8 of 9; 1 photograph not yet named'. On a values tier the Estate Inventory states the total as a floor when any line has no value ('at least $8,350; 3 lines not valued: #20, #23, #26'), as the Court Inventory already does. Change invLineReviewed (require a name), the bulk 'reviewed' branch and _invProgressStamp, plus the EIR footer total.
findings.vnote: On Ashworth, #26 has objectName '' and its Reviewed box was enabled. One press set reviewed=true with no dialog, and Not reviewed went from 4 to 3. Select all on every group, then Mark reviewed, marked all 9 lines. The notice named only the 3 unsure lines. _invReviewStats then read complete (9/9) while #26 had no name and #20, #23 and #26 had no value or disposition. The Estate Inventory, captured via _printDocument, printed 'REVIEWED — all 9 items' and 'Total estimated fair market value: $8,350'. That total is 2400+1800+80+3500+450+120, so it leaves out the 3 unvalued lines. No floor, gap or 'not valued' wording appears anywhere on the page; the three lines show only as '—' under 'Not yet decided 3 items'. Code: invLineReviewed (havellin.html:37222) returns true on r.reviewed alone; the row's box (39830) is disabled only when the line is derived-reviewed; _invProgressStamp (30613). The missing floor is the stronger half: it holds even before review, against CLAUDE.md's rule that a schedule with an unvalued line reports a floor and names the gaps.
findings.vrepro: NEW-verify/v1_ashworth.js -> out/v1.log (e26 box enabled true, reviewed true, dialogs []; STATS complete:true, unnamed [26], noval [20,23,26]; EIR stamps 'REVIEWED — all 9 items', total $8,350); out/v1_eir.html

findings.title: The release request the fiduciaries sign carries agent values nobody reviewed, with no IN PROGRESS mark
findings.where: Releases & signed papers → Approval request → Send request (and Approval Request on the work bar). printApprovalRequest (havellin.html:32310–32587) never reads _invReviewStats or invLineUnsure. Evening Desk p.452: 'Papers print marked IN PROGRESS until every item is reviewed; they are never held back.'
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/05_request.js: Send request on Ashworth drafted and filed the request (saved as out/05_request.html). Line #10 'Walnut dresser … $450 … Sell' is an Agent One name, not reviewed, and its row reads 'unsure'. It went to both representatives for initials. A grep of the page for 'IN PROGRESS|reviewed|unsure' finds nothing. The send asked no question (dialogs []).
findings.tc_impact: The TC follows the guide's order (Send request tonight) before every line is reviewed. The representatives sign a release that states a value and a description no person at Havellin has looked at. The paper never says so, though the guide promises every paper is marked. A discerning executor holding a signed release at $450 for a dresser later valued at $1,400 has an indefensible record.
findings.proposal: Treat the request as a paper. Where any line on it is unreviewed, print the same IN PROGRESS stamp and badge those lines 'not yet checked by your concierge'. Ask once at Send request: '1 line on this request is not reviewed (#10 Walnut dresser, unsure). Send anyway?' Make that a flag, not a block, per 'flag rather than block'. Reuse _invProgressStamp(items) over the request's own items and invLineUnsure for the badge, in printApprovalRequest and sendApprovalRequest's pre-check.
findings.vnote: Send request on Ashworth asked no question and drafted the request. The PDF html (s.pdfs) carries #10 'Walnut dresser … $450 Sell Palm Beach Estate Buyers'. That line is agent-named and unreviewed, and invLineUnsure is true for it. The page has no IN PROGRESS stamp and no review mark. printApprovalRequest (32310–32590) never calls _invProgressStamp or invLineUnsure. The Evening Desk says: 'Papers print marked IN PROGRESS until every item is reviewed; they are never held back.' In the seed, #10's $450 carries no valuedBy. The request prints any fmv regardless of review, so an Agent Two figure would go out the same way. The proposal (a stamp plus a one-time flag at send) is a flag, not a block, which the rules allow.
findings.vrepro: NEW-verify/v1_ashworth.js -> out/v1.log ('request has e10 name true | $450 true | IN PROGRESS false', send dialogs []); out/v1_request.html

findings.title: After a bequest awaiting appraisal is signed out to its beneficiary, the desk still offers to hand it to the appraiser
findings.where: Releases & signed papers → Leaving the property, and the Values & appraisals bar's line. signoutGroups (havellin.html:31662–31665) adds an appraisal_out group for any line with apprId and no figure or waiver, whether or not the line is invRecordedGone. deskFoldState 'values' (48280) repeats it as '1 ready to hand to …'. The person sign-out dialog (openSignoutDialog) shows no appraisal caution.
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/13_person.js: with #7 Grandfather clock (Antiques, $3,500, linked to Carla Mendes, pending) approved by both representatives, 'Sign out 1 to Margaret Ashworth' opened a dialog reading only 'Receipt for Property Released … #7 Grandfather clock …'. It gave no caution. After Sign and file the card reads 'Margaret Ashworth · ✓ signed for: #7' and, below it, 'Carla Mendes · appraisal hand-off · 1 line (#7) · Sign out 1 to Carla Mendes'. The Values bar still reads '1 needs an appraisal, each linked · 1 ready to hand to Carla Mendes'. The record keeps apprId 501 with no figure.
findings.tc_impact: On a pickup day the TC sees two Sign out buttons for one clock and nothing saying which comes first. Either order leaves the desk asking for something that cannot happen: a hand-off for an item already in the daughter's house, or a beneficiary's sign-out with no word that the appraisal is outstanding. Counsel then gets a $3,500 antique released with its appraisal still 'in progress' for ever.
findings.proposal: In signoutGroups, skip appraisal_out for a line invRecordedGone or released to a person or vendor. Show such a line once on the appraiser's row as 'left the property before appraisal: Waive or arrange it where it is'. In the receipt, pickup and donation sign-out dialogs, put a line under any ticked line with invAwaitingAppraisal: '⚠ #7 has not been appraised yet (Carla Mendes, due Nov 5): sign it out anyway?' Make it a flag, not a block.
findings.vnote: Thomas and then Nora were recorded through Record the signed request, each with a filed copy. 'Sign out 1 to Margaret Ashworth' opened the Receipt dialog listing only '#7 Grandfather clock'. It gave no word that #7 is linked to Carla Mendes and not yet appraised. After the pad and Sign and file, e07 is gone (invRecordedGone true) with apprId 501, no appraisal figure and invAppraised false. signoutGroups still returns 'appraisal_out:Carla Mendes ready=1'. The card still offers 'Sign out 1 to Carla Mendes'. The Values bar still reads '1 ready to hand to Carla Mendes'. Code: signoutGroups (31662–31665) adds the appraisal group with no gone test. A hand-off signed there would write a false 'Transferred · Out for appraisal' custody event on a probate estate. The release request did carry the not-yet-appraised caution, so the fiduciaries were told; the defect is what the desk offers afterwards.
findings.vrepro: NEW-verify/v2_signout.js -> out/v2.log ('receipt MODAL … #7 Grandfather clock Signed by …', 'e07 after receipt {…gone:true, groups:[receipt … done=1, appraisal_out:Carla Mendes ready=1]}', RELEASES after receipt shows 'Sign out 1 to Carla Mendes')

findings.title: Close job's question leaves out most open work, and a living job closed with an unauthorised firearm, undecided lines and no hours logged
findings.where: Band → ■ Close job. The confirm is built in applyJobTransition (havellin.html:24612, the sentence at 24653) from closeOpenWorkFlag (24595: rooms, no-recipient lines, lines out with an appraiser) and ledgerCloseFlag (34422: estates only).
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/07b_close.js and audit/NEW/18_close_living.js. Ashworth, with vendors rated: the confirm names only the midpoint, the unsigned ledger and '4 of 4 rooms are not marked cleared … finish the rooms and name the recipients'. No line lacks a recipient. It is silent on 3 lines with no disposition, 1 unnamed photograph and 3 lines awaiting written approval. Hale: the confirm names the midpoint and the rooms only. Pressing OK closed the job (status 'closed'), filed the Contents Record and the ledger, and only then did the band say 'No hours are logged yet'. Left open: #7 Remington shotgun (Distribute, Susan Hale, no written approval), 2 undecided lines, the Contents Record unsigned. Job Admin (17_jobadmin.js) had listed 'Hours logged: none yet — the final invoice cannot issue without them' and 'Contents Record signed by the client: not yet'.
findings.tc_impact: The guide says the TC works down Closing the job, then presses Close job. The one question asked at the moment of closing tells them only about rooms. A firearm with no written authority, items with no destination and an hourly final that cannot be priced all pass unmentioned. The family's Contents Record is filed to Drive as the job's record with 2 items 'Not yet decided'.
findings.proposal: Build the close question from one list. Keep the current items and add, each with its count and first item numbers: lines with no disposition ('the ledger / Contents Record sign-off is withheld'), photographs not yet named, leaving lines without the written approval invWrittenReleaseNeeded requires (firearms named first), appraisals still pending, the Contents Record unsigned on living work (the twin of ledgerCloseFlag), and on an hourly job no hours logged (finalAwaitsHours). Say 'name the recipients' only when noRecip is non-empty. These stay flags, never refusals. Change closeOpenWorkFlag and ledgerCloseFlag, plus the sentence at 24653.
findings.vnote: On Hale, after rating Goodwill and Kodner, jobCloseBlockers was empty. At that moment l07 (Remington shotgun) had invWrittenReleaseNeeded true and invApprovalComplete false; there were 2 undecided lines; finalAwaitsHours was true; and the Contents Record was unsigned. ledgerCloseFlag was '' because it applies to estates only. The single confirm named only the midpoint and '3 of 3 rooms are not marked cleared … finish the rooms and name the recipients'. It says 'name the recipients' although noRecip is empty. OK closed the job (status closed, deliveredOn set) and filed the Disposition Ledger and the Contents Record with 2 lines undecided. Only afterwards did the band say 'No hours are logged yet'. Code: closeOpenWorkFlag (24595) and the sentence at 24653. The proposal keeps everything as flags, so jobCloseBlockers (Decided) is untouched.
findings.vrepro: NEW-verify/v3_hale.js -> out/v3.log (PRE-CLOSE blockers [], l07 needs:true complete:false, awaitsHours 'true'; CLOSE DIALOGS text; AFTER CLOSE status closed, contentsRecord filedHow close)

findings.title: A room-check double can be ticked Reviewed on both lines and then prints REVIEWED, counted twice
findings.where: Row's Reviewed box (_invSetReviewed, havellin.html:37258). Mark reviewed's notice (_invBulkApply, 37385–37389) warns only for lines that left Possible duplicates because of the tick (_leftDup). Room-check links stay after review, so they are never named. _invProgressStamp (30613).
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/16_dups.js: the room check flagged #1 'Cobalt glass vase' and #2 'Cobalt blue glass vase on sideboard' ('room check: plainly one thing'). Ticking both Reviewed gave no question, and the block stayed, correctly. Agent Two had valued both at $120. audit/NEW/16b_dups_paper.js: Set disposition Keep, then Mark reviewed, said only '✓ 6 items marked reviewed.' The Contents Record then printed 'REVIEWED — all 6 items' with both vases listed as kept by the client.
findings.tc_impact: The guide's one rule is 'One Reviewed tick covers it all'. A TC working down Not yet decided ticks rows without scrolling back to the Possible duplicates block. The family or counsel then gets a REVIEWED list with one vase counted twice, and on an estate twice valued. 'Nothing double counted' is the first thing the discerning reader checks.
findings.proposal: Treat an open duplicate as unfinished review. A row with dupWith not dupOK keeps its chip, and its box asks once: 'possible duplicate of #2: Remove one, or Not duplicates?' (Remove · Not duplicates · Tick anyway). Mark reviewed's notice also names every picked line still in a duplicate group, not only those that left one. _invProgressStamp prints 'REVIEWED — 6 of 6; 1 possible duplicate pair open' while any group is open. Change _invSetReviewed, the bulk 'reviewed' branch and _invProgressStamp (read agentDuplicateGroups).
findings.decided_conflict: Auto-merging possible duplicate lines (Decided: do not re-propose). This proposes no merge, only that the review and the stamp ask.
findings.vnote: A fresh living house of 6 photographs, with the room check stubbed to answer [s0, s1] as one vase. Agent Two valued both at $120. Ticking both rows' Reviewed boxes gave no dialog, and the Possible duplicates block stayed (dupWith, not dupOK). Set Keep on all, then Mark reviewed: the notice read only '✓ 6 items marked reviewed.' The Contents Record printed 'REVIEWED — all 6 items' with '1 Cobalt glass vase … kept by the client' and '2 Cobalt glass vase, second view … kept by the client', and no duplicate wording. Code: Mark reviewed's _leftDup (37385) reads only _agDupIndex, the same-name index, so room-check pairs are never named. On an estate the EIR would value the vase twice. The proposal merges nothing, so it does not conflict with the Decided auto-merge rule.
findings.vrepro: NEW-verify/v4_agents.js -> out/v4.log (dialogs on ticks [], 'MARK REVIEWED notice ✓ 6 items marked reviewed.', block still drawn after; CONTENTS stamp 'REVIEWED — all 6 items'); out/v4_contents.html

findings.title: Sending the inventory to the estate attorney cannot be found from the guide or the desk
findings.where: evening-desk-guide.html: neither the package nor the Probate or Trust card is mentioned anywhere (grep 'package|attorney' finds only the request's cc line). The desk has no package control. More ▾ offers 'Share w/ Counsel', which shares the photograph folders only. The one pointer is Job Admin's derived line 'Court Inventory and Disposition Ledger delivered to counsel — press Send probate package at the foot of the Probate card on the Client Dashboard', inside the folded card the guide tells the TC to 'Leave shut mid-job'.
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/08_package.js: desk controls matching package|counsel|attorney|send were only ['✉ Send midpoint invoice', 'Share w/ Counsel', '📧 Send request']. The More menu is ['As-Found Record', 'Court Inventory', 'Trust Schedule', 'Appraisal Worklist', 'Snapshot', 'Share w/ Counsel', 'Revoke', 'Show summary & rollups']. The dashboard carries '📧 Send probate package'. audit/NEW/17_jobadmin.js shows the Job Admin pointer.
findings.tc_impact: One of the TC's evening tasks is 'send the inventory to the estate attorney'. A TC who knows only the guide either presses Share w/ Counsel, believing the inventory went, or prints PDFs and emails them by hand. Either way it skips the package's gaps check, the filing and the record of what counsel received.
findings.proposal: Add a short section to The Evening Desk, 'Sending counsel the inventory': the button's name, where it is, that it waits for a named line and asks about the gaps, and I've sent it. Add one line on the desk the TC can see (under More ▾, or the Closing bar's line on an estate): '📧 Send probate package (on the Client Dashboard) →', opening the dashboard on that card. Keep the one send path; this only adds a way to reach it. Update evening-desk-guide.html and its test.
findings.vnote: The Evening Desk mentions the attorney only as the request's cc; it says nothing about the package or the Probate or Trust card. No desk control names a package, counsel, an attorney or probate (v6 found an empty list with More ▾ pressed). sendProbatePackage is reachable only from probatePackageCardHtml on the dashboard (havellin.html:24187). The one pointer on the desk is estateDeliveryLine's 'press Send probate package at the foot of the Probate card on the Client Dashboard' (35133), inside Job Admin. The proposal is a navigation link, not a second send, so the no-control-twice rule holds. I re-rated it medium: the playbook does document the package, and this is a docs and discoverability gap rather than wrong output.
findings.vrepro: NEW-verify/v6_papers.js -> out/v6.log ('desk controls naming package/counsel []'); havellin.html:18215, 24187, 35122–35134; NEW-verify/guide.txt

findings.title: The package's 'still being built' question counts only named lines, so it disagrees with the desk and leaves out unnamed photographs
findings.where: Client Dashboard → 📧 Send probate package → the confirm. probatePackageGaps (filters live lines to those with an objectName before counting) and the desk's Needs you chips.
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/08_package.js on Ashworth: the confirm said '4 rooms not yet locked, 2 lines with no disposition and 2 lines with no value'. The desk the same evening showed 'Unnamed shots 1 · Not yet decided 3 · No value yet 3' and 'Not reviewed 4' (01_look.js). Unnamed photograph #26 is in neither of the package's counts, and unreviewed lines are not mentioned.
findings.tc_impact: The TC is told two different numbers for one inventory. Counsel receives a package whose covering question never mentioned a photographed item nobody has identified yet.
findings.proposal: probatePackageGaps reads the desk's own counts: Not yet decided (named or not), No value yet, and add 'N photographs not yet named' and 'N lines not reviewed'. The confirm and the desk then quote one set of figures.
findings.vnote: probatePackageGaps(9601) returned ['4 rooms not yet locked','2 lines with no disposition','2 lines with no value']. The desk's chips on the same job read Not yet decided 3, No value yet 3 and Unnamed shots 1. The gap is #26, the unnamed photograph: the function counts only lines with an objectName (code at its 'live' filter), and it never mentions unreviewed lines. I re-rated it low because the confirm goes to the TC, not to counsel, and the package's own pages still print the unnamed line.
findings.vrepro: NEW-verify/v6_papers.js -> out/v6.log (package gaps); out/v1.log CHIPS line; probatePackageGaps in havellin.html

findings.title: A driver's signature on Havellin's Donation Release is recorded as the charity's receipt
findings.where: Releases → Sign out 1 to Goodwill Palm Beach → Sign and file. SIGNOUT_KINDS.donation (havellin.html:31605) files kind 'donation'. invDonationReceipted counts any 'donation' record as the receipt. The Donations card, the Closing bar and Job Admin's 'Donation receipts on file' read it.
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/05c_signout.js: after the driver signed on the iPad, the card read '✓ 1 charity receipt on file: listed on the Donations card'. The Closing bar went from '0 of 1' to '1 of 1 donated line receipted'. The filed sheet (out/05c_signout_sheet.html) is headed 'Donation Release'. It says 'This list records the delivery only; any valuation is the donor's.' It is signed by 'Marcus Reed (Goodwill driver)' on a Havellin form.
findings.tc_impact: The TC never chases Goodwill's own acknowledgement, because the desk already says the receipt is on file. The estate's accountant, or a living client claiming the deduction, needs the charity's written acknowledgement, not a pickup signature on our sheet. The ledger and Job Admin say 'receipted' when they are not.
findings.proposal: Keep the iPad sign-out as proof of delivery. Record it as 'picked up by <charity>' (as a vendor pickup reads), and leave 'receipted' to a charity receipt filed with File charity receipt. Wording: 'Picked up: signed on the iPad. Charity's receipt: not yet filed'. Either file the iPad sheet under its own kind or have invDonationReceipted ignore records with glass:true. Update the playbook's Donations paragraph.
findings.vnote: The behaviour is as described. findings.title: A tick made while a re-value is out is silently undone when the new figure lands
findings.where: Row: rename → Where it goes → Reviewed while agentValueAfterRename's request is out. invLineReviewed (37222) returns false once agentValueUnreviewed holds for the new figure. The box is enabled during the run, and the sub-line reads 'value made for an earlier name'.
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/09_race.js: renamed #1 'Restoration Hardware Belgian linen sofa', chose Keep and ticked Reviewed (chips 'Not reviewed 12'). The held re-value then landed at $1,400 (was $350). The box unticked itself, the chips went back to 'Not reviewed 13', and the only words on screen were the work bar's 'Agent Two: 1 valued · review them below'.
findings.tc_impact: Working down Not yet decided, the TC renames a maker, decides and ticks, as the guide teaches. Twenty seconds later the line is back on Not reviewed with no notice. On a 300-line house they find out only when the count will not reach zero.
findings.proposal: While a line is in _avState.ids or out, disable its box with the title 'Agent Two is valuing it again for the new name'. Or let the tick stand and, when the figure lands, toast '#1 re-valued $350 → $1,400: tick it again', with a 'Re-valued since you ticked' entry in Needs you. Accuracy still wins: the new figure needs its look.
findings.vnote: Renaming s2 to 'Restoration Hardware walnut sideboard' sent an agentValue request, which I held. The box stayed enabled, with the title 'Tick when this line has been checked'. Choosing Keep and ticking set reviewed and valReviewed, and Not reviewed fell to 5. When the held figure landed ($120 → $1,400), _avWrite cleared valReviewed. invLineReviewed went false, the box unticked, Not reviewed went back to 6, and no dialog appeared. The only words were 'Agent Two: 1 valued · review them below'. While the request was out, the row did say 'value made for an earlier name' and the notes list said Agent Two was valuing it again. Unticking is the right outcome, since the new figure needs a look. The fault is that the tick was accepted with no warning at the box. I re-rated it low.

findings.title: A drawer shot piece by piece cannot be made into one line: only removed, leaving one piece's photo as the drawer's
findings.where: Bulk bar (Set category, disposition, valuation source and condition, Move to room, Set recipient, Mark reviewed, Re-value, Approval request, Send request, Record approval, Remove lines, Clear). findings.proposal: Add 'Combine into one line' to the bulk bar. It keeps the first picked line, names it from the shared kind ('Drawer of kitchen utensils: whisk, wooden spoons, can opener, …'), sets Qty 1 and the room, and attaches the other photographs to it as close-ups (detail, groupId = the kept line). findings.vnote: The bulk bar offers Set category, Set disposition, Set valuation source, Set condition, Move to room, Set recipient, Mark reviewed, Re-value, Approval request, Send request, Record approval, Remove lines and Clear. The proposal is a person's explicit act, so it is not the Decided auto-merge, and it keeps removal as tombstones. Two caveats. The auditor's 'value stayed the whisk's $40' is a stub artifact: a rename sends the line to Agent Two again. And turning Items shots into detail shots relabels photographs, which needs care. Agent One's drawer rule makes the case uncommon.

findings.title: 'No signed receipt' is flagged from the moment of approval, while the item is still in the house
findings.where: Releases → the person's row ('⚠ no signed receipt filed for #7') and the bar ('1 signed receipt owed'). invReleasedToPerson counts an approved Distribute line as released.
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/05c_signout.js: immediately after the second representative's signature was recorded, with the clock still in the hall, Margaret's row read '⚠ no signed receipt filed for #7' and the Releases bar 'N signed receipt owed'.
findings.tc_impact: An amber 'owed' that nothing tonight can clear: the receipt is signed when she collects it. It is noise between approval and pickup.
findings.proposal: Read 'ready to sign out' (grey) until the line is recorded as gone, and 'receipt owed' (amber) only after it has left.
findings.decided_conflict: Domain rule (P19): invReleasedToPerson = Distribute and the approval complete or the line recorded as gone. This would key the owed flag on gone only.
findings.vnote: The behaviour is accurate. Right after Nora's signature was recorded, with the clock still in the house, e07 read invReleasedToPerson true and invReceiptOwed true. The row and card read '⚠ no signed receipt filed for #7' and the bar read '1 signed receipt owed'. That is the P19 Domain rule as written: invReleasedToPerson is Distribute with the approval complete or the line recorded as gone, and the playbook says a receipt is owed 'once every fiduciary has approved it, or once it is recorded as gone'. Keying the flag on gone alone changes Anthony's rule.

findings.title: Where it goes uses different words from the camera, in alphabetical order
findings.where: Row's Where it goes select (_invDispOptions): Auction, Consign, Distribute, Donate, Hold, Junk, Keep, Move, Sell. The camera's chips: Keep, New home, To a person, Donate, Sell, Remove, Undecided.
findings.evidence: audit/NEW/03a_dom.js (out/03a_row.html) shows the option order. The Evening Desk has to explain the renames ('New home is Move, To a person is Distribute, Remove is Junk'), and the family's papers print Junk as 'Disposed of'.
findings.tc_impact: Three words for one answer across camera, desk and paper. On a Home Transition the commonest answers (Keep, Move) sit 7th and 8th of 10.
findings.proposal: Order the desk's options as the camera's chips (Keep, Move, Distribute, Donate, Sell, Junk, then Auction, Consign, Hold) and label them with the camera's words where they differ ('Move (new home)', 'Distribute (to a person)', 'Junk (remove)'). Stored values unchanged.
findings.vnote: The row's options come from INV_DISPOSITIONS (havellin.html:27995), which is alphabetical and carries the stored words: Auction, Consign, Distribute, Donate, Hold, Junk, Keep, Move, Sell. The camera's chips (FIELD_DISPOSITIONS, 40593) are Keep, New home, To a person, Donate, Sell, Remove, Undecided. The guide spells out the renames. Relabelling and reordering while leaving the stored values unchanged conflicts with no rule. The guide's test pins the row's words to _invDispOptions, so it would need updating in the same commit.

findings.title: Send request is offered again straight after I've sent it, beside Record the signed request

findings.evidence: audit/NEW/05_request.js: right after I've sent it, with nothing signed back yet, the card reads 'Sent Oct 26 … 3 lines still unsigned', then '[Record the signed request] [📧 Send request]' at equal weight.
findings.tc_impact: A new TC reading 'No Send request: … a drafted request is waiting' as the only case where it hides presses it again. The representatives then get the same request twice the same evening.
findings.proposal: After a send with nothing yet signed, show Send request as a quiet link, 'send it again (e.g. lost in their inbox)', under Record the signed request. Back to a button once a partial signature or a new line makes a fresh request owed.
findings.vnote: Right after I've sent it, with nothing signed back, the card shows 'Record the signed request' and '📧 Send request' together. The auditor's 'equal weight' is wrong: Record the signed request is the filled btn-bronze and Send request is an outline btn-s. Offering the send again is consistent with the guide's 'No Send request' row, because the three lines are still waiting. The remaining friction is mild.
